finding.claim: GET /users has no authentication and takes the org filter from the client, so any caller can list id and name for users in any org (cross-tenant enumeration).
finding.sink: req.pg.query("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1", [req.query.org]) returning rows as JSON (db.js:9-10)

trace.note: app.get("/users") registered with no auth middleware in the chain
req.query.org passed as the org filter; no caller identity or org membership check
all matching id/name rows returned as JSON

finding.guards_checked: Parameterized query ($1) so no SQL injection (case 10 not applicable). No auth middleware or session check in db.js; req.pg is used but not set here, so upstream auth/tenant middleware may exist outside this file. Case 09/27 ownership pattern does not directly match because there is no caller identity to scope against. Confidence medium: exploitable only if no upstream gateway enforces org membership.

verdict.guard_found: none. db.js:8 registers app.get("/users") with no auth middleware. db.js:9 passes req.query.org straight into the parameterized query, so there is no SQL injection, but no caller identity or org-membership check exists. db.js:10 returns every matching id and name as JSON. The app calls app.listen(3002) at db.js:23 with no global middleware. The repo's only file is db.js, so nothing in the codebase sets req.pg or enforces tenant scoping.
verdict.reason: The trace matches db.js:8-10: an anonymous request to /users with an arbitrary org value returns that org's id and name rows (db.js:9-10), and no auth or tenant check exists in the repo (db.js:8, db.js:23). The candidate's residual doubt is that an external gateway might enforce org membership, but nothing in the provided code supports that, and req.pg is also injected from outside this file.
